value.statement: In a Hausdorff topological space, every compact set is closed.

patches.value: Choose R₀ using F001 and define Q=∏_{i=1}^n[-R₀,R₀]. Each coordinate has absolute value at most ‖x‖, hence K⊆Q. M013 and M014 give μ(Q)=∏_{i=1}^n μ([-R₀,R₀])=(2R₀)^n<∞. Apply M018 to the compact K in the Hausdorff Euclidean space to conclude K is closed and hence Borel measurable; monotonicity yields μ(K)≤μ(Q)<∞. As K was arbitrary, Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. The Borel measurable structure on ℝⁿ is the σ-algebra generated by Euclidean opens, so opens are measurable. Joint smoothness and u=q on the open spatial complement of C throughout J imply all first spatial and time derivatives, and the second and mixed derivatives entering e_t, vanish outside C. Thus e(·,t) is continuous with compact support in C. Apply M001 to conclude e(·,t) is integrable. The same smoothness/support argument shows u_t(·,s), u_{x_j}(·,s), e(·,s), and e_t(·,s) are continuous and vanish off C for each s∈J and j=1,…,n. This proves the claimed output for arbitrary t>0.

value.bindings: X=ℝⁿ with its Euclidean topology and Borel measurable space, V=ℝ, μ=Lebesgue measure, f=e(·,t).
hypothesis_checks: ℝⁿ has a measurable space and Euclidean topology.
Its Borel measurable space makes Euclidean opens measurable.
ℝ is a normed additive commutative group.
S001–S002 prove Lebesgue measure is finite on every compact subset of ℝⁿ.
e(·,t) is continuous and has compact support in C by smoothness and H003.
